summary:
AstroFire SI is an interactive Super Intelligence (SI)-powered web dashboard that summarizes, ranks, and interprets all 19 eligible NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) microgravity combustion investigations (ROSES-24 E.12 #7-#25).

Designed for aerospace engineers, researchers, professors, and students, AstroFire SI translates complex ISS and Cygnus datasets (SAFFIRE I-III, BASS, BASS-II, FLEX, FLEX-2, SAME, SAME-R, DAFT/DAFT-2, CFI, SPICE, SLICE, and ACME) into actionable fire prevention, detection, and suppression insights—specifically addressing the >40% relative oxygen increase (>=30% O2 at <=10.2 psi) planned for future Moon Bases and pressurized lunar rovers.
details:
AstroFire SI addresses the critical fire safety challenges of human spaceflight across ISS, Artemis Lunar Gateway, Moon Base habitats (>=30% O2 at <=10.2 psi), pressurized rovers, and EVA spacesuits (100% O2 at 4.3 psi). Key Capabilities: 1. Unified 19-Investigation PSI Explorer: Filters and ranks all 19 NASA PSI combustion studies across four safety pillars—Prevention (SAFFIRE I-III, BASS, BASS-II, ACME BRE), Detection (SAME, SAME-R, DAFT, DAFT-2), Suppression (FLEX, FLEX-2, CFI fine-water-mist and CO2/He dilution), and Partial-Gravity Mimicry (ACME E-Field Flames).

2. Interactive Habitat Atmosphere & Flammability Simulator: Computes relative material flammability indices across Earth/ISS baseline (21% O2, 14.7 psi), Moon Base/Rover target (>=30% O2, <=10.2 psi), ACME CFI-G high-oxygen spherical diffusion regime (up to 85% O2), and EVA Spacesuit (100% O2, 4.3 psi).

3. Partial-Gravity Bounding Model: Bridges the current lack of lunar (0.16g) and Martian (0.38g) partial-gravity combustion data in PSI (ahead of upcoming LUCI and FM2 datasets) by bounding risk using 0g ISS data, 1g counterflow ground studies, and ACME E-Field Flames ion-driven convection data.

4. Terrestrial Tech Transfer Module: Highlights how ISS fine-water-mist extinguishers and SAME multi-moment smoke detection improve firefighter gear and building smoke detectors on Earth.
